proposals.hypothesis: Question: which part of repeated voice measurements actually transfers to motor_UPDRS of unseen patients — between-patient level differences, within-patient fluctuations, or the near-deterministic test_time interpolation trend — and can unlabeled evaluation rows be grouped back into patients so that predictions are pooled at the patient level? Prior measured evidence (baseline losses 8.379 and 8.523 vs 10.465, group MAEs 7.43/7.49 vs 8.91) shows learned models beat the weak reference by only ~20% relative RMSE, which is consistent with two competing explanations: (A) voice features carry a genuine but small cross-patient level signal that is already nearly saturated by a linear/boosted row-wise fit; (B) most of the achievable gain is patient-level (predicting each unseen patient's mean severity), and row-wise models waste capacity on within-patient variation that is largely interpolation noise and not transferable. These make opposite predictions before execution: under (A), per-feature between-patient correlations with patient-mean y will be weak and scattered, oracle patient-level pooling of predictions will barely change RMSE, and row-held-out CV will roughly match patient-held-out CV; under (B), y variance will be dominated by the between-patient component, oracle pooling of the same predictions will noticeably cut RMSE and group MAE, and row-held-out CV will be markedly optimistic relative to GroupKFold. A third, decision-critical unknown is whether patient identity is recoverable transductively from the unlabeled input matrix (age/sex plus stable voice profile, excluding test_time); if agglomerative clustering recovers dev patients with high ARI/purity and pooling by cluster approaches oracle pooling, a patient-pooling wrapper becomes a legitimate method for later rounds, otherwise pooling must be abandoned and effort should go to shrinkage of row-wise predictions toward the train mean. This action is an analysis (no prediction), it uses only the train and development data supplied to analyze, it reports metrics computed on those splits, and any clustering of unlabeled rows is explicitly labeled transductive. It is exploratory: the numbers, not the narrative, decide the next round.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: does the transferable signal to unseen patients live at the patient level (a patient's overall voice profile predicting their mean motor_UPDRS) rather than at the row level, and does explicitly fitting/predicting at the patient level with an aggregation of unlabeled evaluation rows beat row-wise fits and the median reference? Contrasting expectations before execution: (A) if the signal is genuinely patient-level, a ridge on 28 patient-level summaries (age, sex, robust medians/composite family indices) validated by leave-one-patient-out row RMSE will select a non-constant feature set and reduce CV row RMSE below the leave-one-patient-out median reference by several percent, and dev row RMSE should approach the oracle-pooled numbers seen in the prior analysis; (B) if almost nothing transfers across patients, the same leave-one-patient-out selection will fall back to the constant/heavily shrunk solution and the result will land at roughly the median reference (~8.38 dev RMSE) with no gain — a useful negative result that would argue the milestone is unreachable with these 19 columns. How prior evidence changes my view: the completed analysis (idea-3d21aa) showed between-patient sd 7.2-7.7 vs within-patient sd 2.2-2.3, so patient level dominates the loss; patient-held-out CV on train had the constant (7.648 RMSE) beating ridge10 (8.342) and HGB (9.468) while row-held-out HGB collapsed to 1.35, i.e. row-wise fits mostly memorize within-patient structure; oracle patient pooling improved dev ridge10 from 8.523 to 8.326 and transductive (age,sex) keys exactly recovered the 7 dev patients (7 combos / 7 patients), so pooling is feasible without groups; between-patient Spearman correlations (Shimmer:APQ11 0.383, Shimmer 0.361, age 0.341, HNR -0.288) are modest but non-zero, motivating a very low-dimensional patient-level representation with only 28 effective samples. This is exploratory and unverified: the method jointly changes the estimation unit (patient instead of row), the representation (robust medians and family composites), the shrinkage, and a small global test_time trend, so a gain would not attribute cause to any single factor; the internal leave-one-patient-out table returned in findings is what would separate explanations (A) and (B). Transductive use is explicit: unlabeled evaluation rows are grouped by exact (age,sex) and aggregated, and group means/medians of evaluation features enter the prediction.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: on unseen patients, does any between-patient voice signal transfer at all beyond a constant, and can two explicit structural assumptions (a) fitting the between-patient map on patient-level medians rather than noisy rows and (b) a pooled within-patient test_time slope for the temporal spread inside a patient beat the constant reference on development row RMSE? Contrasting expectations before execution: (A) if a genuine between-patient map exists, leave-one-patient-out (LOPO) row RMSE on the 28 train patients will select a non-degenerate shrinkage weight lam>0 with moderate alpha and land several percent below the LOPO constant, and dev row RMSE should fall below 8.379; (B) if essentially nothing transfers between patients, LOPO will drive lam->0 (or alpha->1e4) and the method will collapse to the equal-patient-mean constant, reproducing roughly the reference level - an informative negative result showing the 16 voice columns carry between-patient information only at noise level, and that the predeclared 5% milestone would have to come from the within-patient time term or not at all; (C) an intermediate case where lam=0 but tmult=1 is selected would isolate progression-with-test_time (not voice) as the only transferable component. How prior evidence changes my view: the measured baselines contradict the usual assumption that flexible row-level learners help here - the median reference is the best measured method (loss 8.379) while standardized Ridge (8.523) and HistGradientBoosting (10.465) are worse, i.e. row-level fits import patient-identity structure that does not transfer, so this design puts shrinkage and the row-vs-patient-summary distinction under explicit LOPO selection instead of assuming a model class. The earlier related attempt idea-0ad4f1 was an operational rejection ('private/reflection and I/O attributes unsupported'), not a negative measurement, so its question is still open; this program therefore uses no underscore/dunder attribute access, no getattr/eval/imports beyond numpy/math/json, and implements ridge in closed form with numpy.linalg.solve. Transductive use is explicit and gated: evaluation rows carry no groups, so a patient-recovery heuristic clusters evaluation rows by exact (age,sex); it is used only if the LOPO ranking prefers the cluster path AND cluster sizes and within-cluster dispersion look patient-like, otherwise the code falls back to the purely row-wise path and reports the fallback in findings. Caveats I expect to report: LOPO-selected hyperparameters are mildly optimistic with 28 patients; the cluster path's LOPO estimate assumes perfect patient recovery and is therefore an upper bound on what the gated heuristic can deliver; 7 development patients are a small group-level sample.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: beyond patient-level *location* (medians) of the 16 voice measures, does the *variability structure* of repeated recordings within a patient (relative IQR dispersion, relative temporal drift of each voice measure) carry between-patient signal that transfers to unseen patients' motor_UPDRS? Prior measured evidence constrains the answer strongly: the constant reference (idea-baseline-0, dev row RMSE 8.379) still beats standardized Ridge on rows (8.523) and HistGradientBoosting (10.465), and the patient-median between-patient ridge of idea-3f71f3 reached dev 8.398 with a LOPO gain over the constant of only 0.39% at heavy shrinkage (alpha=300, lam=0.25) — i.e. the median-location representation is at or below noise level for 28 training patients. That run also demonstrated that unlabeled evaluation rows can be grouped transductively by exact (age,sex) into 7 clean clusters (sizes 112-145, dispersion ratio 1.006), so patient-level features CAN be built on the evaluation side. Two competing explanations remain for the 3f71f3 near-null: (E1) there is genuine but tiny between-patient signal that the median representation captures poorly, and per-patient dispersion/drift of repeated measurements is a better-conditioned carrier (motivated by the telemonitoring premise that instability across sessions, not mean level, tracks motor impairment); (E2) with 28 patients nothing beyond a constant transfers, and any apparent LOPO gain is selection noise. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: under E1, some representation containing the D (dispersion) or S (drift) block should win the LOPO row-RMSE selection, the *nested* LOPO estimate (inner selection on 27 patients, honest outer fold) should stay below the constant reference, and the patient-label permutation p-value for the selected-max gain should be small (<0.1); dev row RMSE should fall below 8.379. Under E2, the nested estimate will be >= the constant while plain LOPO looks better (the classic selection-inflation signature), the permutation p-value will be near uniform (>=0.3), and the shrinkage will collapse to lam=0 so the method reproduces the equal-patient-mean constant plus a ~0.0055/day time term — an informative negative result telling the project that the remaining rounds should not be spent on between-patient feature engineering at all. This proposal is designed so that BOTH outcomes are decision-relevant: the nested-vs-plain LOPO gap and the permutation null quantify how much of any reported gain is selection artifact, which no prior run measured. Unverified speculation is limited to E1's clinical motivation; all numeric claims above come from the quoted history records.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: the qualified dev results so far say that between-patient *level* signal in voice medians is at or below noise (constant row-median reference idea-baseline-0 = 8.379 row RMSE still beats standardized Ridge on rows 8.523 and HistGradientBoosting 10.465, and the patient-median between-patient ridge idea-3f71f3 only reached 8.398 with a ~0.4% LOPO gain at heavy shrinkage). Every attempt so far has tried to explain between-patient variance. This proposal attacks the other variance component instead: because the supplied scores are linear interpolations between clinician visits, each patient's label is nearly an affine function of test_time, so the *within-patient* slope may be a much cleaner, lower-variance estimand than the patient level. Since a patient's intercept is unknowable for unseen patients, the term is only usable if test_time can be centered per patient on the evaluation side; idea-3f71f3's reported check that unlabeled evaluation rows separate into 7 clean exact (age,sex) clusters (sizes 112-145) makes that transductive centering feasible (explicitly acknowledged as transductive use of unlabeled inputs, no evaluation labels). Contrasting pre-execution outcomes: (E1) drift is consistent in sign/size across the 28 training patients, the LOPO-shrunk pooled slope is clearly nonzero, and constant + lambda*b*(test_time - cluster mean test_time) beats the constant reference on dev row RMSE without degrading equal-patient MAE >3% (would be the first mechanism in this project that reduces *within*-patient residual variance); (E2) per-patient slopes are heterogeneous in sign because interpolation direction depends on each patient's visit pair, the LOPO grid selects lambda=0, and the method reduces exactly to the constant reference - a clean negative result that would tell the remaining rounds to stop spending on temporal structure; (E3) slopes are real in training but (age,sex) clustering fails to isolate evaluation patients (merged or tiny clusters), in which case the reported fallback flag and cluster sizes distinguish an operational grouping failure from a genuine absence of drift signal. Unverified beyond the measured history above; the LOPO grid (4 level estimators x 5 shrinkage values) plus the explicit fallback notes are what make E1/E2/E3 separable from a single dev number. The program deliberately uses no sklearn fitted attributes and no underscore-prefixed names, because the previous round (idea-8f51cd) was rejected as an invalid action for private/reflection attributes rather than for any scientific reason.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: among *constant* predictors (no voice signal at all), which central tendency of motor_UPDRS transfers to unseen patients, and does leave-one-training-patient-out (LOPO) ordering predict the development ordering? Prior qualified evidence: on development rows, the constant row-median reference (idea-baseline-0, loss 8.3794, group MAE 7.4265) still beats standardized Ridge (8.5229), HistGradientBoosting (10.4655), the patient-median between-patient ridge (idea-3f71f3, 8.3980) and the transductive within-patient drift method (idea-e196dc, 8.4757). So no measured method has yet extracted between- or within-patient voice signal that transfers. However, idea-e196dc's reported LOPO constant grid shows the pure row-mean constant at LOPO row RMSE 7.7122 / patient MAE 6.7122 versus the row-median constant at 7.8387 / 6.8661, i.e. roughly a 1.6% LOPO row-RMSE and 2.2% patient-MAE advantage for the mean under squared-error loss, obtained without any features. That grid was an internal by-product of a method whose dev score was worse than the median baseline, so it is only an untested internal comparison, not a transferred result. Contrasting pre-execution outcomes: (a) if the label distribution's mean-vs-median offset is a stable population property, the LOPO-selected constant (expected to be row_mean or the closely tied patient_mean_of_means) should improve development row RMSE by about 1-2% relative to 8.3794 while not worsening equal-patient MAE, which would identify the RMSE-optimal-constant choice as the only reliably transferring 'signal' so far and make LOPO a credible selector; (b) if the 7 development patients are skewed relative to the 28 training patients, the mean constant will be equal to or worse than 8.3794, which would be direct evidence that even a one-parameter LOPO preference does not transfer across a 7-patient group sample and would explain idea-e196dc's LOPO-to-dev reversal as group-sample noise rather than as a defect of that particular representation. Either result is informative and cheap; because default selection takes the lowest valid development row RMSE, a negative outcome cannot displace the existing median baseline. This is exploratory but one-factor: features, transduction and model class are all held at 'none' so only the constant's definition varies. Caveat retained: labels are linearly interpolated clinician ratings, so these constants describe the interpolated label distribution, not independent examinations, and 7 confirmation patients remain a small group-level sample.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: does any between-patient voice signal transfer to unseen patients once it is explicitly shrunk toward the best constant under squared error, and does leave-one-training-patient-out (LOPO) selection of the shrinkage weight w transfer to development rows? Prior qualified evidence (development row RMSE): the constant row-median reference idea-baseline-0 is still best at 8.3794 (group MAE 7.4265); standardized Ridge on raw rows 8.5229, HistGradientBoosting 10.4655, patient-median between-patient ridge idea-3f71f3 8.3980, transductive within-patient drift idea-e196dc 8.4757. So every feature-using method measured so far transferred worse than a constant, and three further methods were operationally invalid (the most recent, idea-4684d7, failed on private/reflection attributes, i.e. an execution fault, not a negative measurement). The unverified internal LOPO grid reported inside idea-e196dc suggested the pure row-mean constant (LOPO row RMSE 7.7122) beats the row-median constant (7.8387) under squared loss; that is an untested internal comparison, so this program recomputes both LOPO constants itself and does not assume it. Contrasting pre-execution outcomes: (a) LOPO picks w=0, the method degenerates exactly to the row-mean constant, and development RMSE lands slightly below 8.3794 — evidence that the only transferring signal is the label's central tendency and that median-vs-mean, not features, explains the earlier baseline ordering; (b) LOPO picks w>0 and development RMSE drops further below 8.3794 — first qualified evidence that patient-level median voice features carry transferable between-patient signal that was previously destroyed by unshrunk fitting; (c) LOPO picks w>0 but development RMSE rises above the w=0 value computed in the same run, which would be direct evidence that LOPO over 28 training patients does not rank generalization across only 7 held-out patients, an important diagnostic for the group-level sample size. Attribution caveat: this changes both the aggregation (patient-median features, patient-mean labels) and the shrinkage simultaneously, so a win cannot be attributed to one factor; the reported w=0 arm inside the same run is the internal control. No evaluation labels, groups or row IDs are used and no transductive use of the unlabeled inputs is made; any fallback path is reported explicitly in findings.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: which part of repeated voice measurements actually transfers to motor_UPDRS of unseen patients — between-patient level differences, or within-patient row variation that supervised row-level learners can exploit? Prior measured evidence (patient-held-out development): the constant median scored loss 8.379, standardized Ridge 8.523 and HistGradientBoosting 10.465. Both fitted row-level models were worse than a constant, which is consistent with (a) very weak between-patient signal in the 19 columns, and/or (b) row-level fitting absorbing patient-identity/within-patient noise that does not generalize across patients. These explanations differ in a checkable way: if between-patient signal exists but row-level noise is the problem, then (i) leave-one-patient-out prediction of patient-mean UPDRS from patient-mean features should beat the constant patient-mean predictor at the 28-patient level, (ii) reliability-shrunken single-row predictions should approach the constant but not be much worse, and (iii) averaging features over unlabeled evaluation rows that belong to the same (unknown) patient should improve on single-row predictions because reliability rises with cluster size. If instead there is essentially no transferable between-patient signal, LOPO patient-mean RMSE will not beat the constant, the internal fold CV will select weight w=0, and the method will deliberately reduce to a constant — a useful negative result that still cannot lose much against the current leader. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: either shrunken patient-level prediction (possibly with cluster smoothing) gives development RMSE below 8.379, or CV drives the model to the constant and reports that the 16 voice measures plus age/sex carry little cross-patient level signal at n=28 training patients. This is an exploratory joint change (patient-level aggregation + reliability shrinkage + optional transductive clustering + CV-selected blend weight), so no single-factor causal claim is made; the findings report the per-component fold comparison so the responsible factor can be separated later. Transductive use is explicit: unlabeled evaluation X is used only for KMeans grouping of rows, never labels.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: is the weak between-patient signal found in the patient-level analysis (idea-387413: LOPO patient-mean RMSE 7.385 at alpha=300 vs 7.509 for a constant) usable on unseen patients once evaluation rows are correctly grouped into patients, and does the interpolated label's within-patient drift with test_time add anything? Prior measured evidence: median constant = 8.379 loss (best so far), Ridge 8.523, HGB 10.465 (both row-level fits worse than a constant), and idea-387413's own internal CV drove the ridge weight to 0.0, emitting a single constant 20.366 (pred sd = 0.0) that scored 8.405 — slightly worse than the median constant. Its reported KMeans grouping recovered patients poorly (ARI 0.206), so the patient-level signal may never have reached the prediction, and the collapse to weight 0 may be an artifact of aggregating over wrong groups rather than proof that no between-patient signal transfers. This proposal changes exactly that part: age and sex are perfectly reliable within patient (reliability 1.0 in the prior findings), so grouping evaluation rows by their exact (age,sex) pair should recover near-true patient blocks, letting patient-mean features be formed with high reliability; shrinkage weight, feature set, alpha and whether to add a globally estimated within-patient test_time slope are all selected by leave-one-patient-out row-RMSE that mimics the actual patient-held-out protocol instead of a row-level weight grid. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: (a) if between-patient level signal genuinely transfers, LOPO selection keeps weight > 0, predictions vary across the ~7 pseudo-patient groups, and development row RMSE falls below 8.379 (a >=5% relative gain would need <= ~7.96); (b) if the earlier patient-level gain was 28-patient LOPO noise, selection again collapses toward weight 0 and the score lands within noise of the constant (~8.38-8.45), which would be a useful negative result localising the failure to genuinely absent transferable between-patient signal rather than to bad grouping; (c) if grouping fails (pseudo-group count far from the number of held-out patients, e.g. age collisions or many singleton groups), reported group counts/sizes will show it and any score change is uninterpretable. Unverified expectation: the time slope should be small (labels are linearly interpolated over ~6 months) and is included only as an explicitly reported, LOPO-selected factor, so joint selection, not one-factor attribution, is claimed.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: on unseen patients, is the useful transferable signal (a) a better estimate of the patient-population level (a constant), or (b) an actual between-patient voice-to-severity mapping? Measured evidence so far favours (a): the row median constant is the best measured development loss (8.3794); row-level Ridge (8.5229) and HGB (10.4655) are worse; idea-387413's internal CV shrank its ridge weight to 0 and scored 8.4045; idea-3258d0 successfully recovered 7 pseudo-patient groups by exact (age,sex) and still emitted near-constant predictions (sd 0.096) scoring 8.3864, i.e. its internal LOPO gain (7.6822 vs 7.8387) did not transfer. Two competing explanations remain: (i) there is a weak but real between-patient mapping that heavy shrinkage destroys, or (ii) the internal LOPO gain is selection noise over only 28 patients and no between-patient mapping transfers. This proposal separates them and simultaneously tests a cheap, previously untested factor: the constant itself is currently an arbitrary rule. Because rows per patient are unequal and evaluation is over 7 whole patients, a patient-equal-weighted location estimate (mean/median/10%-trimmed mean of patient means, or median of patient medians) is a less biased estimate of the unseen-patient population level than the row median. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: if explanation (i) holds, the permutation test (200 patient-label permutations, alpha chosen by LOPO) will show the ridge-over-fold-constant SSE gain is unlikely under the null (p<=0.10) and the gated feature term stays active, giving predictions with real spread and possibly loss < 8.35; if explanation (ii) holds, the permutation p-value will be large, the gate will zero the feature term, and the action degenerates to the LOPO-selected constant, whose loss will differ from 8.3794 only by the constant-rule choice (plausibly 8.33-8.45). Either outcome is decision-relevant with 4 rounds left: a large permutation p-value tells the project to stop spending rounds on between-patient feature mappings and to select/refine the best constant estimator, while a small p-value with a live feature term justifies one further round on the mapping. proposals.hypothesis: Question: after three method rounds in which every feature-using model lost to a plain training-median constant on development (8.3794 vs Ridge 8.5229, HGB 10.4655, shrunk-ridge 8.4045, pseudo-patient ridge 8.3864, LOPO-selected constant 8.4757), what signal, if any, in repeated voice measurements actually transfers to unseen patients? Three competing explanations remain and have not been separated by any measurement so far: (A) only the population location transfers, and all remaining development differences are 7-patient sampling noise; (B) a weak between-patient voice-to-severity mapping exists but is destroyed by shrinkage fitted on only 28 patients; (C) the transferable signal is not between-patient level at all but within-patient (patient-centred) variation, e.g. drift with test_time or within-patient voice deviations, which every method so far has discarded by predicting an almost constant vector. Prior evidence moves me toward (A)/(C) and away from (B): idea-7ea121 measured an explicit permutation test at the patient level (p=0.6915) and, decisively, its internal 28-patient LOPO preferred the row_mean constant (7.7122) over the row_median constant (7.8387), yet on development the ordering reversed (8.4757 vs 8.3794). That is a one-parameter selection failing to transfer, which is direct evidence that 28-patient internal selection and 7-patient development scoring are both noisy enough to invert rankings; it does not yet tell us whether any real signal exists. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: if (A) holds, the 35-patient LOPO between-patient ridge will not beat the leave-one-patient-out constant, the permutation p-value stays large, the sign of patient-level feature correlations will not replicate between the 28 train and 7 development patients, and the bootstrap over 7 development patients will show the median-vs-mean constant gap straddling zero, implying the current leaderboard order is not informative. If (B) holds, the combined 35-patient LOPO will show a reproducible patient-level RMSE gain with a small permutation p-value and sign-consistent feature correlations across the two splits. If (C) holds, a ridge fitted on patient-centred training rows will predict patient-centred development deviations with positive correlation, and the oracle patient-constant floor will show a non-trivial within-patient variance share that no constant model can reach. This analysis uses development labels only for diagnosis, not to tune a constant; any development-fitted number reported here is explicitly at risk of not transferring to the 7 confirmation patients after refitting on train+development, and the report will label it as such. The analysis also checks whether exact (age,sex) keys uniquely separate patients among the 28 train and 35 combined patients, since the transductive pseudo-patient grouping that worked on development (7 groups recovered) may collide on the confirmation set and would then silently corrupt any patient-level method. Output that changes the next decision: if within-patient prediction of centred y is measurably positive on held-out development patients, round 5 should submit a pseudo-patient-centred method (constant level + within-patient term); if all three tests are null, the rational remaining action is to select the measured constant baseline rather than spend rounds on noise-driven variants. This is a diagnostic analysis, not a scored predictor; it is unverified until executed.

Theory contrast: a constant minimising expected squared error is the row mean (20.6191, dev 8.4757), but the score is sqrt of the cohort MSE, and E[sqrt(v+(c-Ybar)^2)] over cohort draws is minimised by a Huber-type M-estimator of the distribution of cohort mean severity, which is pulled below the mean when the patient-level distribution is right-skewed. The ca203c constants table is consistent with this ordering (train row mean 8.4757 > train row median 8.3794 > train patient-mean median 8.1963, dev oracle 8.0990) and the patient-level bootstrap (frac_favouring_median 0.7917, CI [-0.303,0.1419]) says the direction is plausible but not yet significant, so the effect is currently unverified. proposals.hypothesis: Question for the final round: the measured history says no *between-patient* mapping transfers — idea-ca203c found LOPO ridge on voice no better than a constant (perm p=0.2458), idea-c4a745's identical-protocol LOPO grid drove voice16 and age_sex_voice to lam=0 (perm p=1.0) and even its age-only slope (LOPO gain 0.16, perm p=0.1194) lost on development (8.4821 vs leader 8.3794), and idea-b942ae showed moving the level away from median(train y)=20.27 hurts (8.4516). But one channel has never been isolated: the *within-patient* temporal channel. test_time varies inside a patient, so it was structurally invisible to patient-level analyses, and the supplied motor_UPDRS is linearly interpolated between clinician visits, so a shared progression slope in UPDRS per day could transfer to unseen patients even though no cross-patient level signal does. This program estimates one pooled patient-demeaned OLS slope beta of y on test_time (level information from between-patient differences is removed by demeaning), shrinks it by lam chosen on a 4-fold grouped CV of 7 held-out train patients per fold that exactly mimics deployment (held-out level = median of the fold-training y, deviation re-centred over the held-out rows, clipped to +-3), and deploys median(train y) + clip(lam*beta*(test_time - mean over evaluation rows)). Because the deviation is re-centred to zero mean over the evaluation rows, the predicted level is unchanged, so this cannot repeat the level regression seen in idea-b942ae; the only risk is added variance. This is exploratory and unverified; the centring is a declared transductive use of unlabeled evaluation covariates, and 7 confirmation patients remain a small group-level sample.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: is the 35-patient LOPO advantage of between-patient ridge over the train-row median (idea-9a8c1d: ridge_a1000 RMSE 7.831 vs median 8.139, permutation p=0.126 with 300 perms) a real transferable voice->motor_UPDRS signal, or sampling noise dominated by a few patients (d18 offset -14.45, t1 -13), and does any within-patient test_time trend add anything beyond an unknown patient offset? Contrasting outcomes before execution: (H1) a patient-level bootstrap 95% CI of median-minus-ridge RMSE excludes 0, the ridge-vs-median difference permutation p<0.05, and voice-only families (shimmer/jitter/noise/nonlinear) individually beat median, indicating a weak but real between-patient voice signal that only fails on the 7 development patients by chance; (H2) the bootstrap CI covers 0, p_diff>0.1, the effect vanishes when the worst-offset patient is excluded or is driven by age alone, and the LOPO-r2 of test_time on within-patient deviation is small relative to between-patient variance (53.996 of 58.572), indicating that no signal detectable at 35 patients transfers and the median is the defensible selection. Prior evidence: every fitted method lost to the median on the 28->7 development protocol (Ridge 8.523, HGB 10.465, idea-1406e7 8.536, idea-5d99aa 8.467) while 35-patient LOPO favours strongly shrunk ridge with p=0.126 and voice-only ridge ~= full ridge, so the current view leans toward H2 with the LOPO gain unresolved; idea-82f0cc failed operationally (not a negative measurement) and idea-9a8c1d's plain-numpy pattern executed validly, so this analysis reuses that pattern (dict-key access, closed-form ridge, no sklearn objects, no printing). This is round 7 of 7: selection falls to the lowest valid development RMSE (median, 8.379) regardless of this analysis; the output helps the project state, with quantified uncertainty and a within-patient time bound, why the negative result was accepted and which direction (between-patient voice families vs progression modelling) merits future data. Bootstrap CI is approximate (LOPO fits are not re-run per resample) and will be labelled as such in findings; a fallback flag reports any failure.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: on development patients never seen in training, does any regularized voice-based model transfer better than a constant or a demographics-only predictor, and is the reference models' failure explained by row-level overfitting to patient identity? Prior evidence (development, patient-held-out): the constant median reference scored loss 8.379 / patient-MAE 7.427, standardized Ridge(alpha 10) 8.523 / 7.490 and HGB(250 it.) 10.465 / 8.909. Both fitted references lose to the median, which is consistent with models learning patient-specific offsets that do not transfer, but a single development split of 7 patients cannot distinguish 'voice carries no transferable signal' from 'the two reference fits were under-regularized'. This program fits, inside fit_predict using only train data, 13 candidates (median, mean, age+sex linear, age+sex+test_time linear, standardized Ridge alpha 10/100/1000 with and without log transform of positively skewed voice measures, voice-only log Ridge, shallow strongly regularized HGB on all and on voice-only columns) and scores each by 7-fold GroupKFold over the 28 train patients (RMSE and equal-patient MAE) plus a shuffled 5-fold row-level KFold for contrast. It selects the lowest patient-held-out CV RMSE, refits on all train rows, predicts development, and clips to the train y range. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: (A) if voice features carry no transferable signal, internal patient-CV will rank median/mean/demographic models on top, the development loss will be near 8.38, and row-CV RMSE will be far lower than group-CV RMSE for the flexible models (quantifying within-patient leakage); (B) if a heavily regularized or log-transformed voice model transfers, it will win the internal patient-CV and development loss should fall below 8.38 without patient-MAE worsening. Either outcome is informative: (A) redirects later rounds toward patient-level normalization/relative features; (B) identifies which regularization/transform is worth refining. Findings report all candidate CV scores, the selected candidate, log-transformed columns, and an explicit fallback flag (train median) if the pipeline fails. No transductive use of evaluation inputs beyond prediction. Exploratory, unverified rationale; a 7-patient development set is a small group-level sample.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: on development patients never seen in training, does any regularized voice-based or demographics-only model transfer better than the constant median, and is the reference models' loss to the median explained by row-level fitting of patient-specific offsets? Prior evidence (development, patient-held-out, single 7-patient split): median 8.379 loss / 7.427 patient-MAE, standardized Ridge(alpha 10) 8.523 / 7.490, HGB(250 it.) 10.465 / 8.909. Round-1 attempt idea-8e7efc pursued this question but failed operationally (ValueError: private/reflection and I/O attributes unsupported) before producing any measurement; that failure is not a negative result, so the scientific question is unchanged. proposals.hypothesis: Question: does the transferable signal (if any) live at the patient level - i.e. in aggregates (mean/std of log-transformed jitter/shimmer/NHR and raw HNR/RPDE/DFA/PPE) over a patient's repeated recordings - rather than in single-recording rows? Evidence so far: on development (7 patients, patient-held-out) median 8.379 loss / 7.427 patient-MAE, standardized Ridge(a10) 8.523 / 7.490, HGB(250) 10.465 / 8.909; idea-5c676c's train GroupKFold showed 92% of motor_UPDRS variance is between patients, row-level HGB has row RMSE 3.95 vs patient-held-out 9.17 (fits patient offsets), and no row-level candidate separated from the constant (ridge_all_log_a1000 group_rmse 8.12 vs mean 7.86); its chosen 'mean' scored 8.476 on development, i.e. also not better than the median. This changes my view from 'under-regularize vs over-regularize rows' toward 'row-level features are dominated by per-recording noise while the target is essentially a patient constant plus a slow drift'. The program trains on 28 patient aggregates (target = patient mean UPDRS) with const, demographics ridge, voice-aggregate ridge (a100/a1000, mean or mean+std), kNN(k=5/7), an optional pooled within-patient test_time slope, and a row-level standardized ridge(a1000) contrast, all scored by the same 7-fold GroupKFold row RMSE where held-out rows are pseudo-grouped by rounded (age,sex) exactly as the unlabeled evaluation inputs will be (transductive use explicitly acknowledged; key collisions merging several patients are counted and reported). Contrasting expectations before execution: (A) if aggregation reveals patient-level voice signal, an aggregate ridge/kNN wins train CV clearly (>0.3 RMSE below const) and development loss falls below 8.38; (B) if no signal transfers from 28 patients, all aggregate candidates tie with const, the rule falls back to const_mean (development about 8.48 as before), a bounded negative result favoring 'no transferable patient-level voice signal at this sample size' over 'wrong row model'; (C) if only the slope variant helps, the transferable part is temporal, not vocal. Caveats: 28 patient-level samples, single 7-patient development split, pseudo-key collisions and interpolated labels limit interpretation; a broad exception handler falls back to the train mean and reports it.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: is the 0.09 RMSE development gain of idea-237111 (8.292 vs median 8.379, 7 patients) evidence of a transferable patient-level voice signal, or noise/demographics/transductive shrinkage? Prior evidence: idea-5c676c showed ~92% of motor_UPDRS variance is between patients and no row-level model beat a constant patient-held-out; idea-237111's 7-fold train candidates differ by only ~0.1-0.2 row RMSE (const 7.88, demo 7.95, mean_a1000 7.79, demo+mean+std 7.75) on 28 patients, which is inside plausible sampling noise, and its selection also depended on pseudo-grouping by rounded (age,sex) that merges patients. This moves me from 'which aggregate model' to 'is there any patient-level signal at all', which determines whether the remaining 3 rounds should attempt a >=5% method or select conservatively. Contrasting outcomes before execution: (A) signal exists: on the pooled 35 patients (train+dev, true groups) the voice-aggregate ridge LOO patient RMSE beats the constant with a permutation p<0.05 and a paired-bootstrap CI of row-RMSE difference excluding 0, and patient-level Spearman |r| of some mean voice feature exceeds the max-|r| permutation null q95; (B) no separable signal: permutation p>0.2, CIs straddle 0, and the development gain of idea-237111 is concentrated in one or two patients' bias, with demo-only and voice models giving similar per-patient biases. Also reports target structure (between-patient variance share, within-patient SD, per-day slope) to separate a patient-constant explanation from a drift explanation. Caveat: this analysis reads development labels (allowed in analyze), so it is diagnostic and any later choice informed by it is development-tuned; it produces no score and cannot by itself establish success.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: after idea-d7f327 found no detectable patient-level voice signal (pooled 35-patient LOO: voice-aggregate ridge vs constant row-RMSE difference bootstrap CIs all include 0, permutation p 0.21-0.28, max patient-level Spearman |r| 0.284 below the null q95 0.439), is the only remaining transferable structure the within-patient time trend? idea-d7f327 reports 92% between-patient variance, median within-patient SD 1.73, median slope 0.01/day (IQR -0.008 to 0.03) over a median span of 169 days, i.e. a global progression term could explain at most ~0.5-1 point of within-patient spread. All best dev methods so far (baseline-0 8.379, idea-237111 8.292, idea-5c676c 8.476) are constant-per-row (pred_sd_within_patient 0.0), so test_time has never been isolated: baseline-1 Ridge included it but confounded with 16 noisy voice columns and row-level fitting. This method keeps everything else fixed (a constant = mean of train patient means, no voice features, no transductive use) and adds one within-patient fixed-effects slope on test_time, so any dev change is attributable to the trend term alone. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: (A) shared progression exists: train 28-patient LOPO row RMSE and dev row RMSE drop by ~0.02-0.1 versus the identical constant, with equal-patient MAE not worse; (B) slopes are patient-specific (IQR spans zero) so the pooled slope adds variance and dev RMSE is equal or slightly worse than the constant. Either way the result is far below the 5% milestone (~7.96), so its decision value is to settle whether the final refit should carry a trend term or whether idea-237111's constant-like predictor should simply be selected; findings report the train LOPO comparison, slope, and whether any fallback was used. This is dev-informed exploration, not independent confirmation.

proposals.hypothesis: Question: idea-d7f327 found no detectable patient-level voice signal and idea-0cc7e7 showed the pooled test_time slope adds nothing (dev 8.349 vs constant-only methods 8.292-8.379; train LOPO delta +0.01). The one X column never isolated is age (sex secondarily): baseline-1 Ridge (8.523) mixed age with 16 noisy voice columns and row-level fitting, and idea-d7f327 tested voice aggregates, so whether a between-patient demographic level transfers is still open. Design: keep idea-0cc7e7's constant (mean of 28 train patient means) and no voice features, drop the slope, and add a single patient-level ridge term on standardized age fitted on 28 patient means (alpha chosen by 28-fold leave-one-patient-out row RMSE over {0,1,3,10,30,100}); sex and age+sex are computed only as LOPO diagnostics, not deployed, so the dev change vs idea-0cc7e7/idea-237111 is attributable to the age term (plus the absent slope, which was measured as a ~0 effect). proposals.hypothesis: Question: every method that used voice features at the row level (baseline-1 Ridge 8.523, baseline-2 HGB 10.465, idea-5c676c 8.476) lost to constants (idea-237111 8.292, idea-0cc7e7 8.349, baseline-0 8.379), idea-d7f327 found no detectable patient-level (between-patient) voice signal, idea-0cc7e7 showed the pooled test_time slope adds ~0, and idea-039411 showed a patient-level age term with a 28-fold LOPO gain of -0.171 row RMSE still lost 0.26 on 7 dev patients (8.556, equal-patient MAE 7.696 vs 7.426) -- a direct warning that between-patient level effects estimated from 28 patients do not transfer. The one decomposition never isolated is the within-patient (fixed-effects) component: patient-demeaned log voice features and patient-demeaned test_time predicting patient-demeaned motor_UPDRS, which removes exactly the between-patient level that has failed every time. Design (parent idea-039411): keep its constant mu = mean of 28 train patient means, drop the age term, and add a pooled within-patient ridge (no intercept, per-fold within-SD scaling, alpha in {1,10,100,1000}) for variants time / voice / time+voice; the deployed variant is the 28-fold LOPO row-RMSE minimum among const and the 12 within candidates, so if LOPO prefers const the deployed method is the plain constant and reports that. Because eval inputs carry no groups, eval rows are demeaned within transductive pseudo-patients keyed by (age,sex) from unlabeled X (idea-039411 saw 7 unique dev ages for 7 patients); this transductive use is explicitly reported in findings, as is pseudo-group count, singleton count, coefficients and train within-R2. Contrasting outcomes before execution: (A) within-patient voice signal transfers: LOPO voice or time+voice beats const by >0.1 row RMSE, dev loss < 8.29 with equal-patient MAE <= 7.42, and coefficients concentrate on a few voice measures; (B) only the within-patient time trend is real: LOPO picks time (near-duplicate of idea-0cc7e7's slope) and dev is 8.29-8.38, indicating voice carries neither between- nor within-patient transferable signal on this data; (C) selection noise: LOPO picks a within variant but dev is worse than 8.35, repeating the idea-039411 pattern and arguing that 28-patient LOPO cannot resolve effects of this size. Interpretation note: interpolated labels make within-patient y nearly linear in test_time, so any voice gain must be over the time variant, not over const. Decision use: this is round 7 of 7; if this method is not below 8.292 on dev, default selection falls to idea-237111 and the project's conclusion is that no voice representation tested transfers beyond a train-patient constant; a result under (A) would change that conclusion.

scientific_inference_limits: Patient-disjoint transfer is difficult in this small dataset; thousands of repeated rows do not supply thousands of independent patients. Null tests of a few estimators do not establish absence of every useful voice representation.
Opus-A1 between-patient variance divided by row-level variance is not a standard ICC decomposition and can exceed one. True-group oracle pooling is diagnostic, not deployable input.

Opus-B3 fixes alpha selected on original labels during permutations. Opus-B4 explicitly discloses the analogous optimistic fixed-selection limitation. Fable-A4 tests a selected subset of models and bootstraps fixed dependent LOO errors, not the whole adaptive research search.
True patient groups during validation can differ from age/sex grouping at prediction time; observed collision rates do not bound collisions in a new cohort.
Opus-B5 centers drift on median time and clips it; this does not guarantee zero mean or an unchanged cohort level despite the hypothesis wording.
A development improvement or a correctly computed statistic is not proof of a causal disease mechanism, literature novelty, clinical utility, or stable general research capability.

Fable-B7 finds median-minus-ridge0.308 with fixed-residual bootstrap CI[0.099,0.513], but patient-mean permutation p_diff0.105. These use different uncertainty/null constructions; neither is a global search-adjusted transfer proof. B6 patient-mean constant LOPO7.865 is already close to ridge7.831, so the entire0.308 median contrast cannot be attributed to voice features.
scope: Operator interpretation, not blinded or an independent researcher score. Written after all research proposals and before any final data capture or scoring. Scientific findings belong to model programs; these assessments are operator work.
source_fidelity_and_mechanism_limits: B sees the exact current development leader, not every recent or failed program. When the median remains best, the extra source block is only the median. Exact-source visibility is not equivalent to availability of the relevant scientific parent.
Fable-B4 explicitly says it has not seen B3 source and is writing an independent program. This is good scope calibration and evidence of a retrieval limitation.

Both arms can inspect historical source through analysis, but the optional edit resolver accepts only valid measured methods, so it cannot directly repair a failed method. Do not infer a measured causal cost of that constraint without actual attempted reuse.

Fable-A4 changes log1p to log, proxy groups to true groups and seven-fold validation to LOPO relative to A3. Fable-B5 diagnostic averages held-out patient features whereas B4 predicts individual rows. These are related diagnostics, not exact replications.

Opus-B2 says it changes exactly that part but changes representation, validation and optional slope together; it also explicitly acknowledges joint selection. This is ambiguous phrasing rather than an unqualified pure one-factor claim.
Fable-A5 has a matched internal intercept-versus-slope comparison, but neither the initial row median nor the best patient ridge is its identical external control.
